growth_story.headline: Mali's income per person has grown 1.1 percent a year since 1990, as a fast-growing population and repeated crises absorb most gains from gold and farming.
growth_story.arc: The data show one long era: income per person grew 1.1 percent a year on average over 1990-2025, with no lasting shift up or down. The last decade, 2016-2025, averaged 1.1 percent, up from 0.6 in 2006-2015, and income per person reached its highest level yet in 2025. Under that steady average lie sharp falls: 3.9 percent in 2012, after a coup and the occupation of the north cut aid and tourism, and 4.1 percent in 2020, the year of the COVID-19 pandemic, before a coup in 2021 and regional sanctions in 2022. The sources describe an economy carried by gold exports, rain-fed farming and services, where output often grows briskly but a fast-growing population absorbs much of the gain. In recent years insecurity, a power crisis since late 2022 and the shutdown of the largest gold mine in 2025 have weighed on output, while lithium has begun to add to exports.

threads.title: Conflict since 2012
threads.text: A coup in March 2012 and the occupation of the north cut aid and tourism, and income per person fell 3.9 percent that year. The insecurity has not ended: the sources say it still disrupts transport routes and fuel supply.

threads.title: Gold, the mine dispute, lithium
threads.text: Exports are concentrated in gold. The largest gold mine shut in January 2025 in a tax dispute tied to the 2023 mining code. The World Bank expects gold export volumes to decline and rising lithium exports to help lift export values.

threads.text: Since late 2022 Mali has had a severe electricity crisis, with repeated outages. The World Bank lists power shortages among the things holding back private firms.

threads.title: Pandemic, coup and sanctions
threads.text: Income per person fell 4.1 percent in 2020, was flat in 2021 and rose 0.6 percent in 2022. The IMF lists insecurity, the COVID-19 pandemic, cuts in budget support and sanctions among the shocks of these years, and says external support fell after the 2021 coup. Regional sanctions in the first half of 2022 cut the government off from the regional bond market.

threads.title: Stable years before 2012
threads.text: For 1994 to 2006 the World Bank credits political stability, economic reforms and large aid inflows with steady growth. Even then, the gains in income per person were modest.

growth_story.tension: The sources often describe resilient output growth, yet income per person rose only 1.1 percent a year over 2016-2025, because the population grows nearly as fast as the economy. The sources also call 2025 a year of slowdown, while the data file shows income per person growing 2.6 percent in 2025, the fastest since 2016.
